title: Kunti
hook: before the war, Kunti gives Krishna a message for her sons, and the message is a story about another mother who would not let her son lie down

segments.voice: Yesterday, Kunti at Ekachakra, offering one of her own sons to repay the family who sheltered them. Did you do something small for someone who once took you in? Day one thousand three hundred thirty-seven.

Krishna's peace mission has failed. Before he leaves Hastinapura, he goes to see his aunt, who has stayed behind in the city while her sons waited out their exile. He asks if she has a message for them. She does. But she doesn't start with advice. She starts with a story, an old one, she says, about a woman named Vidula and her son. Kunti wants her sons to hear it before the war. Today, at the end of a week of the epics' women, Kunti speaks through someone else's voice.
screen: `THE PEACE MISSION HAS FAILED.` → `A MESSAGE FOR HER SONS.` → `SHE TELLS THEM A STORY.`

segments.voice: The story is in the Mahabharata's Book of Effort, and here it is in paraphrase. Vidula is a proud woman of a warrior family. Her son Sanjaya has been beaten by a rival king, and now he lies at home, low and listless, doing nothing. Vidula goes to him, and she is not gentle. Get up, she tells him. You were not born to lie here. And then this line. In Sanskrit it runs muhurtam jvalitam shreyo, na tu dhumayitam ciram: better to blaze up for a moment than to smolder for a long time. Burn brightly, even briefly, she says, rather than smoke. Her son argues back. What good will a kingdom be to you, he asks, if I'm dead? She answers him again and again until he rises. Then Kunti adds her own words to Krishna, for Arjuna and Bhima: the time has come for which a mother of warriors bears sons. Notice three things. First, it's a mother choosing hard words. Kunti, who asked Krishna for trouble in the Bhagavata, here asks her sons to walk toward it. Second, it's her voice through another woman's. She doesn't only command; she tells a story and lets it work. Third, it's not a comfortable passage. Some readers hear courage; others hear the cost of a war that a mother has just urged. The epic keeps both. And it closes a week of women. Sita, answering Rama before the army. Draupadi, keeping accounts, waiting by an empty pot, asking for a killer's life. And Kunti, who sends a story ahead of her sons.
screen: `VIDULA AND HER BEATEN SON` · `BLAZE A MOMENT, DON'T SMOLDER` · `KUNTI SPEAKS THROUGH THE STORY` · `A WEEK OF THE EPICS' WOMEN`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: find the smolder. Sit comfortably and let the breath settle. Ask, gently: is there one thing in my life that's been smoking for a long time? A call I keep not making. A task I keep not starting. Don't scold yourself. Vidula's words were for a warrior; yours can be kinder. Just let the thing come clearly into view. With each breath in, let a little warmth gather around it, the way an ember brightens. With each breath out, let one first step appear. If you pray, you can ask for courage. The bell holds the time.
Kunti. Before the war, she sent her sons the story of Vidula: better to blaze for a moment than to smolder for a long time. Today's word.
Your line: Kunti. Today, take one small first step on something that's been smoldering, the way Vidula's son finally got up. Day one thousand three hundred thirty-seven.

howItsDone: Hindus meet Kunti's message and the story of Vidula in fuller retellings and commentaries on the Mahabharata's Udyoga Parva, where it is read as a lesson about courage and duty.

fork.setup: you're Kunti. peace has failed, and Krishna asks what to tell your sons. what do you send?
options: a plea to avoid the war at any cost.
the story of Vidula and her son.
fork.reveal: she sends the old story of Vidula rousing her beaten son, and adds that the time has come for which she bore them.

original.script: मुहूर्तं ज्वलितं श्रेयो न तु धूमायितं चिरम्
original.say: moo-HOOR-tum JVUH-li-tum SHRAY-yoh nuh too dhoo-MAH-yi-tum CHI-rum
original.note: Sanskrit, from Vidula's words to her son: better to blaze up for a moment than to smolder for a long time.

trapdoor: what you thought: Kunti's message would be a mother's plea for peace.
what it means: she sends a story of a mother who rouses her son to stand up.
what a scholar hears: muhurtam jvalitam shreyo, na tu dhumayitam ciram, from the Vidula passage of the Udyoga Parva.

notes: Week end (days 1331–1337): the teach closes with a look back at Sita, Draupadi and Kunti. Sita is recalled only by name, without restating day 1331.

Confirm the Vidula passage: Sanjaya defeated by the king of Sindhu; Vidula's line 'muhurtam jvalitam shreyo na tu dhumayitam ciram' (Critical Edition 5.131.14, approx.); Sanjaya's reply about what use a kingdom would be if he died; Kunti's added words to Arjuna and Bhima that the time has come for which a kshatriya woman bears sons.
